cases.basis: production: a bench brainstorm of many turns carried durable facts inside its requests and Haiku wrote none; every other case is short

turns.author: person
turns.speaker: alana
turns.text: Help me think through a workbench. A knock-down Moravian, maybe five feet long, is the design I keep seeing.

turns.author: ashley
turns.text: A Moravian is a good first big build if you're patient. The usual path is a laminated top from construction-grade 2x12s, a leg vise on the front left and a row of holdfast holes along the back. Five feet is a sensible length: long enough for most furniture parts, and it comes apart to move. Do you want to start with the top, since everything else is measured from it, or with the base?

turns.author: person
turns.speaker: alana
turns.text: Base first, I think. Oh, and it has to go in the basement, and the sump pump sits in the back corner so I can't box that in. What wood for the legs?

turns.author: ashley
turns.text: Leave about a foot of clear floor around the pump and the bench can still sit against the back wall. For legs, laminate four 2x6s of Douglas fir or southern yellow pine into 5 by 5 inch posts. They're cheap, stiff and heavy, which is the point of a bench. Dry them in the house for a couple of weeks first so they stop moving. Flatten each lamination before glue-up, because a twisted leg is very hard to fix after.

turns.author: person
turns.speaker: alana
turns.text: Fine, pine it is. I'll probably do the glue-ups on Sunday mornings, that's when I have the basement to myself and Elodie's still asleep. What's a decent glue for that, I don't want to rush it?

turns.author: ashley
turns.text: Titebond III gives you about ten minutes of open time and holds up in a cool basement, which matters in winter. Dry-fit everything, mark the order of the boards, and have clamps set to width before you open the bottle. Don't glue more than two or three boards at a time on a first attempt.

turns.author: person
turns.speaker: alana
turns.text: Makes sense. How many clamps does a top that long need?

turns.author: ashley
turns.text: For a five-foot top you'd want a clamp roughly every ten to twelve inches, so around six for each glue-up, alternating above and below to stop the panel bowing. If you have fewer you can do it in stages: glue two boards, let them cure, then join the halves. It's slower but it works. Pipe clamps are the cheapest way to add more.

turns.author: person
turns.speaker: alana
turns.text: Okay, staged. Next, the vise. I'm left-handed, so the leg vise goes on the front right, flip whatever you'd normally suggest. Can you put together a shopping list of everything for the base?

turns.author: ashley
turns.text: Mirrored for a left-handed bench: leg vise on the front right, holdfast holes biased towards the left end. Base list: four 2x6x8 pine for the legs, two 2x6x8 for the stretchers, a box of 3/8 inch lag bolts with washers for the draw-bored joints, a quart of Titebond III, and a half-inch drill bit for the dog holes. Want me to add it to the shopping list?

turns.author: person
turns.speaker: alana
turns.text: Yes, add all of that to the shopping list.

turns.author: ashley
turns.text: Added. That's the full base list on your shopping list.

expect.states: The basement has a sump pump in its back corner that must not be boxed in
Alana is left-handed
Alana has the basement to himself on Sunday mornings
Alana is building a five-foot knock-down Moravian workbench in the basement
